⚡ SUNDAY METALS PULSE — SEPTEMBER 27 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

The week ends with a fascinating divergence:

Industrial metals are screaming SUPPLY.

Precious metals are fighting the FED.

☢️ URANIUM

Another week, another reminder that the nuclear fuel cycle is getting strategic.

Framatome just signed the first commercial contract to supply >5% enriched fuel to an operating US reactor.

X-energy’s new US TRISO fuel facility also reached another construction milestone.

Meanwhile Niger signed an agreement clearing the way toward restarting development of the Madaouela uranium project.

More reactors.
More advanced fuel.
More enrichment capacity needed.

And Kazatomprom recently warned it could easily sell ALL its uranium production into Eastern markets.

The West still needs to secure its pounds.

⚡ COPPER

This is where things are getting VERY interesting.

Copper is hovering around $15,000/t.

Shanghai warehouse stocks have collapsed roughly 70% since June.

LME available stocks are tightening.

The cash market has flipped into backwardation.

Chinese import premiums are near four-year highs.

Yes, Escondida has restarted after its disruption.

But the bigger problem remains:

Copper inventories are piling up in the US while metal becomes increasingly scarce elsewhere.

AI + grids + electrification are colliding with years of insufficient mine investment.

🥈 SILVER

Silver ends the week around $64.

But underneath the price weakness, physical supply keeps throwing up warning signs.

Endeavour Silver’s Guanaceví mine just suffered a ball-mill failure.

Processing capacity:

Normal → ~1,100 t/day
Now → ~600 t/day

Repairs are expected to take around THREE WEEKS.

Meanwhile:

COMEX registered silver remains below 100 Moz.

India is returning to the physical market.

Mine supply remains essentially stagnant.

2026 is still expected to mark the SIXTH consecutive global silver deficit.

Solar thrifting is real.

So is the deficit.

The next thing I want to see?

Investment demand accelerating while inventories keep falling.

That could change this market FAST.

🥇 GOLD

Gold ends the week around $4,275 after another tough week.

The culprit isn’t difficult to find:

US 10Y >5%.
Sticky inflation.
Hawkish Fed.
More rate hikes being priced.

Gold is now down sharply from its 2026 highs.

But here’s the paradox:

The very forces hurting gold today — enormous debt, high borrowing costs, geopolitical instability and persistent inflation — strengthen the longer-term monetary case for owning it.

The battle is simple:

5%+ yields vs monetary insurance.

For now, yields are winning.

🔥 MY SETUP FOR NEXT WEEK

☢️ Uranium — watch contracting and spot activity. The fuel-cycle buildout continues.

⚡ Copper — watch LME/Shanghai inventories. Physical tightness is becoming difficult to ignore.

🥈 Silver — watch COMEX registered stocks and Indian demand. Below 100 Moz keeps my attention.

🥇 Gold — watch US yields. A reversal from 5% could change sentiment quickly.

The common denominator?

SUPPLY.

You can print money.

You can build another data center.

You can announce another reactor.

But you cannot manufacture uranium, copper, silver or gold overnight.

That’s why I keep watching my four metals.

Every. Single. Day.

Astro Teller and I went deep into how moonshots are actually built. His framework starts with a huge problem, not a technology, and combines the audacity to pursue something unlikely with the humility to assume you are probably wrong. 

We talked about why teams should attack the hardest assumption first, what he calls “training the monkey” before building the pedestal, and why the worst outcome is not failure, but allowing a zombie project to consume years of time and capital. 

Astro also shared how AI is reducing the cost of reaching a moonshot and shortening the distance between a crazy idea and the evidence that it might actually work.

Ben Lamm gave us a fascinating look at where biology is heading. We talked about Colossal’s work to bring back entire populations of extinct species, not simply individual animals, and why he believes tens of thousands of mammoths could ultimately be possible. 

We discussed artificial wombs, with Ben predicting that Colossal could birth mammals fully ex utero within 24 months, as well as the growing ability to engineer genotypes, use AI to understand complex biological patterns, and run thousands of simulated experiments before entering the lab. 

His broader point was just as important: if we back up everything else that matters to us, why aren’t we building the infrastructure to back up species?

𝗕𝗶𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗿

“I have given a name to my pain, and it is Batman.”

— The Joker, in the 1989 Batman film

Hello, everyone,

This month, pain came for us too.

The Joker named his pain Batman. We named ours $MRNA.

We cowards saw storm clouds gathering over the markets and decided to take shelter. We concentrated the portfolio in stocks that should fall less when the market drifts down.

In our field, these are lower-risk stocks because they have already passed the pivotal stage, received approval, or successfully launched their products.

The patent cliff is here, and the big companies need sales now. So these stocks are currently among the main acquisition targets.

And then $MRNA happened to us.

The company’s unexpectedly successful Phase 3 trial in adjuvant melanoma set off not only $MRNA, but the other “dream stocks” too.

Where did the money come from to fund the party? You guessed it: the very stocks we ran to for shelter.

Don’t worry, we’re not here to take your livelihood, lie on the couch and cry while you scribble God-knows-what on paper and mutter “Mmm…” or “Where does that meet you?” as the clock ticks.

We’re here to show you the stocks caught in the slaughter that we believe—based on our own position and from the most subjective point of view possible—will deliver very strong returns once the $MRNA frenzy passes.

Here’s our lineup. The figures show each stock’s discount to the industry, based on 2030 multiples that currently stand at around 11.75x:

$VTRS (47%), $JAZZ (42%), $MDGL (28%), $BBIO (48%), $PRAX (55%), $TGTX (22%), $ABVX (23%), $VERA (59%), $MLYS (51%), $BMRN (45%), $GERN (84%), $IONS (32%), $NBIX (39%), $SNDX (41%), $GRFS (57%), $UTHR (30%), $FMS (49%), $AXSM (41%).

These healthcare stocks, spanning a range of sectors and company sizes, trade at an average discount of 44%. In other words, they would need to rise about 80% to reach industry multiples.

Every year that passes widens the discount, since these companies are growing faster than the industry.

Also, 13 of the 18 have a built-in option in the form of a possible acquisition.

So we’re banging the table: buy yourself a basket of these high-quality, relatively safe and very cheap stocks.

That said, to be fair, this is not a risk-free position in the short term. The trend described above could continue.

It’s a trend driven by retail investors, and those cowboys are a law unto themselves.

Also, by the end of the year, $MRNA is expected to report Phase 2 results in NSCLC and Phase 3 results in RCC.

These are “cold” tumors, with low immune activity, so the odds of success are significantly lower than in melanoma, which is a “hot” tumor.

But if either trial works, that’s more fuel on a fire we really don’t need.

Some also argue that at an $80 billion valuation, the market is already pricing in a very high chance of success in these trials. But tell that to our grandmother, because, as we’ve said, if the trials succeed, $MRNA will take off.

“So you’re saying we should buy call options on the stock?” you ask.

A January call option costs $40, or about 67% of the underlying share price on an annualized basis.

In other words, it’s the most expensive option we’ve ever seen—and it’s on an already overvalued stock.

Did we give you a headache in the five minutes you spent reading this? Now try to imagine what we’re going through these days…

And on that cheerful note, we wish you happy holidays (and high returns). Good night.

"
